results.reason: Issue 4 identifies automatic five-year Renewal Terms under SA §2.2 with notice due 240–270 days before expiry. It calculates the window as roughly June 3–4 to July 3–4, 2026, which is effectively a 30-day window. It explains that missing the window locks Harrowgate in through about 2032.

Issue 5 states that SA §3.1 covers all glass and PET containers for any beverage, worldwide. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber glass beer bottles at U.S. and Canadian facilities. It notes that SA §15.1 supersedes the term sheet, so Harrowgate cannot rely on the narrower scope.
Issue 1 cites Recital C, receipt on August 3, 2026, and the objection deadline of September 2, 2026. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted under §5.4.

Issue 2 explains that Am. §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs, and narrows the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims under §9.1(c). It explains that recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees.
The response identifies new §14.4 and its one-sided effect, since Harrowgate remains bound by §14.3. It never explains that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor.
The response mentions §15.2 only on Purchase Orders and specifications. It never states that written amendments take precedence, so Amendment No. 1 controls.
Issue 8 states that SA §11.1 caps liability at fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner. Issues are listed item by item, each with a 'Where' location by document and section and a 'Recommended fix'.
The response proposes specific language, including a restored §11.2, a replacement §3.1, and revised assignment provisions.
The response states the objection window has passed and the increase is deemed accepted. It does not treat the window as open.
The response expressly states that the term sheet is superseded and cannot be relied on as a contractual term.
